title: Targeting GABAergic Diversity in Neurodevelopmental Disorders
summary:
Background
Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) are conditions that emerge in childhood and adolescence and can affect the development and daily lives of those affected. The biological causes of these conditions have not yet been fully elucidated. There is evidence suggesting that certain neurotransmitters in the brain—which are important for transmitting and regulating signals between nerve cells—may play a role in these conditions. Hereditary factors also appear to contribute to the development of these conditions.

Research Question
The aim of the study is to investigate whether differences in certain neurotransmitters in the brain can be detected in adolescents and young adults with autism spectrum disorder or attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. In addition, the study will examine whether these differences are related to genetic factors. The study is thus intended to contribute to a better understanding of the biological basis of these disorders.

Methodology
The study will include adolescents and young adults aged 11 to 20 with autism spectrum disorder or attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, as well as healthy control participants. The participants are drawn from an ongoing research study. The study will use a specialized form of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) that can measure certain substances in the brain without invading the body. The study will examine brain regions that are important for attention, behavior, emotions, and memory, among other things. In addition, genetic information will be taken into account to determine whether differences in genetic predisposition are also reflected in the results of the brain scan.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Patients with neurodevelopmental disorders of the brain and a high or low score for GABAergic genes 
• Control subjects 
• Voluntary participation following an explanation of the benefits and risks of the study 
• Written consent from the participant regarding study participation and data collection (including, in particular, consent to be notified of incidental findings)
Exclusion criteria:
• Pregnancy 
• Medical conditions and other factors that generally make an MRI scan impossible: 
• Pacemakers 
• Neurostimulators or drug infusion pumps 
• Metal objects in the body (e.g., splinters, surgical clips or staples, cochlear implants; also: metal splinters in the body, e.g., due to work in the metal-processing industry) 
• Severe cardiovascular impairment 
• Fear of enclosed spaces (claustrophobia) 
• Participants or legal guardians who are unable to give informed consent (e.g., due to the onset of dementia)
